## ✅ What actually matters today

- **Nvidia board opens investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over ties to Chinese spy**
  *What happened:* Nvidia's board of directors launched an independent inquiry into CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair with an executive who is accused by US officials of gathering intelligence for Beijing.
  *Why it happened:* US security agencies raised concerns that confidential information may have been targeted through the relationship.
  *Why it matters:* Nvidia is the anchor of the global AI boom; management turmoil or national security sanctions could disrupt hardware supply chains worldwide.
  *Who is affected:* Tech investors, AI software developers, and global chip suppliers.
  *What happens next:* Congressional committees plan to hold oversight hearings while Nvidia's board evaluates executive leadership options.   *What happened:* Tesla confirmed it will permanently halt Cybertruck assembly at Gigafactory Texas by mid-2027 and refund deposit holders, while expanding its driverless Robotaxi service to San Antonio today.
  *Why it happened:* Production bottlenecks and sluggish sales forced Tesla to pivot manufacturing lines toward lower-cost autonomous passenger vehicles.

  *Who is affected:* Cybertruck reservation holders, EV buyers, and ride-hailing users in Texas.
  *What happens next:* Gigafactory Texas will undergo tooling modifications through 2027 to prepare for high-volume Cybercab manufacturing. ## 🛡️ Scams & safety alerts

- 🔴 ACTION NEEDED — **Gold bar courier scam targeting senior citizens**
  *How it works:* Scammers pose as FTC or federal law enforcement agents, warning retirees their bank accounts are compromised. They instruct victims to convert cash savings into gold bars and hand them to a courier at a local restaurant using secret passcodes like "tulip" [[U.S. News Today on Fox News]](https://www.foxnews.com/us/fake-federal-agents-push-seniors-turn-savings-gold-bars-couriers-collect).
  *What to do:* Federal agencies, banks, and law enforcement will **never** ask you to purchase gold bars or hand cash to couriers. Hang up immediately and call your bank's official support number [[U.S. News Today on Fox News]](https://www.foxnews.com/us/fake-federal-agents-push-seniors-turn-savings-gold-bars-couriers-collect).

## 🎓 Today's lesson

- **Offer for Sale (OFS) vs. Fresh Issue in an IPO**
  When a company goes public through an Initial Public Offering (IPO), it raises capital using two main methods: a **Fresh Issue** or an **Offer for Sale (OFS)**.
  - In a **Fresh Issue**, the company creates and sells brand-new shares. The money raised goes directly into the company’s bank account to expand factories, hire staff, or pay off corporate debt.
  - In an **Offer for Sale (OFS)**, existing shareholders—such as founders, venture capital funds, or parent companies—sell their personal shares to the public. The money raised goes straight into the pockets of those selling investors; the company itself receives zero cash.
  - *Everyday example:* If a local bakery issues new stock to buy a second oven, that is a Fresh Issue. If the original founder sells part of their own ownership stake to buy a house, that is an OFS. Checking the split in an IPO prospectus shows whether your investment is funding company growth or letting early owners cash out [[Indian Television Dot Com]](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxNWVNxT2lQVjBKU211aUxBN2pONVlUOGozTlc2a0JDcnpXZlZmVXZ4ZjI4a3JHeU9YVHZrRnliVWRBMGdndUZyXzZMOXoyNHE3LWFNX3Via3cwZUJKZzZhREdLNjlMOXJyTkM5ckRzaldqTmttX0V5b1ZUc0tQWHJBQzgyc3NyQ3luNkE?oc=5) [[Free Press Journal]](https://news.google.?oc=5).
